messages.text: Hey. I bought a miner from here. Came bugged. Screen flickered. Got it to stop after months, but can't get it to start mining. I have it connected to pool apparently, but can't see it on the wifi section
Used the customer-care skill
Used the chat-interview skill

Sorry it's been a fight. Most likely: it's sitting on your router's 5 GHz band or still in its own setup AP, so it never joined the network you're looking at. Fix is to reflash the wifi settings on a 2.4 GHz SSID only, plain WPA2, no spaces in the password, then reboot the unit.

What does the miner's screen show right now, an IP address or the setup/AP name?
it showed my wifi when booting up to connect, then now it shows doge and ltc price(hammer miner dco6), temp and mining power of 0 rn cause not runnning

Good, that means it's online, the price ticker only updates with internet. So this is the pool config, not wifi.

On the DC06 the usual culprit is the stratum line. It needs a scrypt merge-mining pool (LTC/DOGE), the port for scrypt, and the worker as yourwallet.workername with any password like x. A Bitcoin pool address will connect and never hash.

What pool address and port did you put in, and what's the worker field set to?
dutch pool. No clue on port. Had someone who knew this more do that, as I can't edit the settings due to no hammer wifi showing up

Right, the Hammer's own wifi only appears when it isn't connected to a network. Since it's online, you get to the settings through your browser instead.

Open your router's client list, find the Hammer's IP, then type that IP into a browser on the same wifi. That's the same settings page. The screen on the unit will often show the IP too if you cycle through it.

Can you get into your router page, or want me to have JD walk you through it?
Do u know what the name would come under in client list?

I don't want to guess the exact hostname on your firmware. It's usually something like "hammer" or an ESP-style name, but it varies.

Easier trick: unplug the miner, refresh the client list, then plug it back in. The entry that disappears and comes back is yours.

If that's fiddly, I'll get JD, who handles the hardware, to walk you through it directly. Want me to?
Found it

Nice. Type that IP into a browser on the same wifi and you'll land on the settings page.

Once you're in, check the pool section: it should be a scrypt merge-mining stratum address with its scrypt port, worker set to your LTC wallet address plus a worker name, password x. Save and reboot.

What does the pool field show now?
it's my doge address in there and I see what pool I want and etc

That part looks right then. The bit that usually kills it is the port, since each pool uses a specific one for scrypt, and a wrong port connects to nothing.

Grab the stratum URL and port straight from Dutch Pool's own getting-started page and paste both in exactly, then save and reboot.

One thing to check on their side: some merge pools want an LTC address as the username and pay the doge separately. Does their page say doge addresses are accepted?
Seems all good. Thanks

Good stuff. Give it a few minutes after the reboot and the hashrate should climb off zero. If it stays at 0, come back and I'll get JD on it.

Before you go, one thing: the screen flicker took months to settle, what finally stopped it?
idk what stopped it because I'm not the one who fiddled with it

Fair enough.

Then one more: what made you hand it to someone else rather than bring it to us when the screen was flickering?
I heard they were good with it and I thought I would have to pay helium to fix it

Worth knowing for next time: asking us costs nothing. A faulty unit goes through the RMA form and we send a return label, no charge. One caveat, if a unit's been overclocked or modified, that's not covered.

Last thing: what gave you the impression a fix would be paid?
I feel like I saw something about setup cost on the site

That's useful, thanks. I'll pass it on so someone can look at where that reads as a charge.

Enjoy the doge. Come back if the hashrate stays flat.
